text:
marta: FYI deploybot just auto-sticky-pinned runtime-3.3 for 'highmem' model set after a surge of OOMs. We need a short plan for targeted unpinning during the maintenance window.

deploybot: [automated] sticky pin created. pin_id=pb-2025-02-12-01. Affected: model-set 'highmem' (llama3-xl, gptx-big). Trigger: OOM spikes >4% (10m). See https://redwood.internal/pins/pb-2025-02-12-01 for details.

sasha: Can we avoid a blunt unpin? Many dedicated customers on these hosts. Prefer canary first and limit to read-only/light eval routes.

tom: Agree. Telemetry shows the regressions are concentrated on large-context (>16k) batch jobs. Suggest scope: limit unpin to max_seq<=8192 and exclude dedicated pools.

kyle: I'll add ephemeral dashboards and a quick eval harness. Also propose an auto-decay that converts sticky->soft after 4h if crash rate <1.5%.

marta: ops, can the deploybot support scoped unpin with exclude filters? We need an exclude for 'dedicated' pools.

ops-sre-bot: Yes. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pinning. Example command: `deploybot unpin --pin pb-2025-02-12-01 --scope region:us-west --traffic-filter 'max_seq<=8192 AND route:!=dedicated' --mode canary`. Monitored metrics: `oom_rate`, `crash_rate`, `p95_latency`, `cpu_util`.

sasha: Rollback criteria proposal: oom_rate <= 0.5% AND crash_rate <= 0.5% for 20m AND p95 latency increase < 7% vs baseline. If fail -> immediate re-pin.

tom: Suggested schedule: canary unpin in us-west at 02:00 UTC -> monitor 20m -> decision at 02:25 -> if green expand to us-east 03:00 -> full unwind 04:00. Fallback: route traffic to runtime-3.2 for affected routes if instability.

kyle: I'll push a synthetic load to the canary hosts after unpin to validate both performance and correctness. Will post script here.

marta: can someone update release notes & the incident log? We should mention sticky pin, affected models, and unpin plan. Sasha?

sasha: on it. Draft note: "Runtime 3.3 sticky pin applied to highmem models following OOM regressions. Scoped canary unpin planned; customers on dedicated pools excluded. See runbook."

ops-sre-bot: Ops checklist:
1) label canary hosts: `pin_canary=pb-2025-02-12-01`
2) execute canary: `deploybot unpin --pin pb-2025-02-12-01 --scope region:us-west --traffic-filter 'max_seq<=8192 AND route:!=dedicated' --mode canary`
3) monitor metrics for 20m (`oom_rate`, `crash_rate`, `p95_latency`) and run kyle's synthetic test
4) on failure -> `deploybot pin --pin pb-2025-02-12-01 --force` and notify #customers-impacts and oncall.

kyle: synthetic test (to run post-unpin):
```bash
# quick sanity driver
siege --concurrency=50 --time=120 "https://canary-host/api/generate?max_seq=1024&model=llama3-xl" > canary-run.log
# smoke-checks: p95 and error rate
cat canary-run.log | jq -s '[.[]] | {p95: .|map(.latency)|sort|.[int(length*0.95)], errors: map(select(.status!=200))|length}'
```

sasha: I'll DM the top 3 dedicated customers with a heads-up about the window (we excluded dedicated but transparency).

marta: Approve schedule and canary plan. Deploybot: schedule canary unpin at 02:00 UTC and await channel ack. React with :white_check_mark: to confirm.

deploybot: Ready to schedule. React to confirm.

ops-sre-bot: tagging the oncall rotation for overnight: @tom will be primary, @kyle secondary.

tom: I'll be online for the 02:00 canary and will post results here.

kyle: ack. I will post dashboard links once ready.

sasha: release note updated and incident log entry created.

marta: thanks all. We'll run the canary and reconvene here with result snippets. If anything deviates, we roll back quickly.
